name: Technical Stand-Up
description: Stand up safely from seated or supine guard without feeding a front headlock. The technical stand-up is the foundational movement for escaping to standing from any bottom position.
shortInstruction: Post one hand on the mat, bring the same-side foot to that hand, drive through the foot and hand to stand, and keep the other hand up in a defensive frame. Face the opponent as you stand.
summary: The technical stand-up is a sequential movement from seated or lying to standing: (1) post your hand on the mat beside your hip, (2) bring your same-side foot to meet your hand, (3) drive through the posted hand and foot to lift your hips, (4) bring your other foot under you as you rise, (5) establish a defensive stance facing the opponent. The technical stand-up is essential for guard recovery, turtle escape, and standing to pass.
whyItWorks: The tripod base (one hand, one knee, one foot) provides stability throughout the stand-up sequence
Facing the opponent as you stand prevents them from taking your back or attacking with a front headlock
The technical stand-up uses the strongest muscle groups (glutes, quads, hamstrings) to lift your body weight
The raised hand provides a defensive frame against takedowns and strikes
commonMistakes: Posting both hands flat and trying to stand — this leaves no arm to defend the back take or front headlock
Standing up with your back to the opponent — this exposes the back for the easiest back take of their life
Standing up tall instead of staying in a grappling stance — a tall posture is easy to takedown
Bringing the foot to the knee instead of the hand — the foot must meet the hand for proper leverage
coachingCues: Hand on the mat, foot to the hand
One hand up, one hand down
Stand in a stance, not tall
safetySummary: Do not post with a straight locked arm — keep the elbow slightly bent to prevent hyperextension
If the opponent shoots as you stand, be ready to sprawl immediately
Practice the technical stand-up slowly before using it under pressure — rushing leads to loss of balance

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The technical stand-up is a sequential movement from seated/lying to standing: Post → Foot → Lift → Base → Stand → Stance. Facing the opponent throughout prevents back exposure and front headlock entries.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent is standing over you while you are seated or supine
decisionTree.action: Execute the technical stand-up: post your hand on the mat beside your hip, bring the same-side foot to meet your hand, drive through both to lift your hips, bring the other foot under you, and stand facing them.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent pushes you back down as you start to stand
decisionTree.action: Drive harder through the posted foot — do not drop back to the mat. The power comes from your glutes and quads, not your arms.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent tries to pass as you stand
decisionTree.action: Keep the defensive hand up and circle away from their attack. The raised hand provides a frame against takedowns.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent shoots a takedown as you stand
decisionTree.action: Sprawl immediately — your defensive hand is already up to post on their back. The technical stand-up puts you in a strong sprawling position.

decisionTree.condition: You keep falling backward during the stand-up
decisionTree.action: Your foot is too far from your hand — bring it closer (within 2 inches of the posted hand). The tripod base requires the foot and hand to be close.

exitStrategies: If you cannot get up, your hand post is too far from your body — bring it closer to your hip.
If they take your back as you stand, you turned away from them — face them throughout the entire stand-up sequence.
If the technical stand-up is not possible (opponent has pinned your legs), use the combat base or granby roll instead.

moneyDetails: The technical stand-up is the most important movement skill in BJJ — it is used in every guard recovery, turtle escape, and scorable stand-up
Mastering the technical stand-up prevents the most common positional loss: back exposure from bad stand-ups
The technical stand-up is the foundation of all wrestle-up systems
fixItFast: If you fall backward: bring the foot closer to the hand before lifting
If they push you back down: drive harder through the foot, do not drop back to the mat
If they try to pass as you stand: keep the defensive hand up and circle away from their attack
